title: Anthropic IPO Raises $81.3 Billion Ahead of Nasdaq Debut
summary: The Anthropic IPO priced at $83 a share, above its $70 to $78 range, raising about $81.3 billion. Shares are set to debut on Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday.
body_markdown:
The offering is expected to close on November 20, subject to customary closing conditions, and the underwriters hold a 30-day option to buy up to 147 million additional shares, Anthropic said.


## Where Will Anthropic Stock Trade?


Anthropic's stock is set to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT, according to the company's release. U.S. stock futures rose on Wednesday evening as investors assessed the pricing, with Nasdaq 100 futures up 1.3%, S&P 500 futures up 0.8% and Dow Jones futures up 0.4% as of 8:22 p.m. ET, according to[Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/wall-street-futures-climb-ahead-of-anthropics-15-trillion-mega-ipo-5037518) .


In Wednesday's regular session, the Dow fell 1.1%, the S&P 500 slipped 0.2% and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.4%, Investing.com reported. The outlet described the listing as a test of investor appetite for AI companies after a recent tech and semiconductor selloff that raised questions about valuations and returns on AI infrastructure spending.


> "The whole AI sector has sold off from its July peak," Jay Ritter, an IPO expert at the University of Florida, told CBS News.


Renaissance Capital senior market strategist Matthew Kennedy told CBS News the deal is "so central to the AI thesis."


## What Is Anthropic Worth?


At the $83 offering price, Anthropic's fully diluted market cap sits at around $1.5 trillion, according to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-ai-offering-price.html) . CBS News reported that the valuation is below the $2 trillion some IPO experts had projected earlier this year.


Anthropic generated $33.24 billion in revenue in the nine months ended September 30, up roughly 1,200% from the same period a year earlier, and its run-rate revenue was roughly $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from the previous month, per CNBC. The company reported a $104 billion net loss for the nine-month period, mostly due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities, compared with a $25.1 billion loss in the same stretch of 2025.


Third-quarter revenue came in at nearly $17 billion, up 45% from the second quarter, according to a regulatory filing cited by[CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/anthropic-ipo-ai-boom-nasdaq-debut/) . Anthropic also carries $6.2 billion in debt, which it calls "substantial," and has committed to nearly a trillion dollars in chips and AI infrastructure through 2045, CBS News reported.


## How the $81.3 Billion Raise Compares With SpaceX


According to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-ai-offering-price.html) , the raise surpasses SpaceX's June IPO, which raised $75 billion initially and a total of $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their overallotment option. Investing.com called the deal one of the largest IPOs on record.


## What the Offering Means for AMZN, GOOGL and NVDA


Amazon and Google both own stakes in Anthropic valued at over $100 billion, according to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-ai-offering-price.html) . A group of tech companies including Google, Microsoft,[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) and Advanced Micro Devices has agreed to collectively invest $26 billion at the IPO price, CNBC reported, and CBS News also named Broadcom among the companies in that investment.


Anthropic is also a buyer of costly systems from Nvidia, Google, Amazon and AMD, per CNBC. The listing follows Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia last week, which rattled investors, CBS News reported.


## Risk Factors in the ANT Prospectus


Anthropic's prospectus includes more than 90 pages of risk factors, and the company has had two high-profile disputes with the U.S. government this year, according to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-ai-offering-price.html) . "It could be hard for management to execute," Ritter told CBS News. CNBC also noted that OpenAI has confidentially filed for an IPO and has said a debut is likely in 2027.
